paper.title: Machine learning for improved density functional theory thermodynamics
paper.file_name: 43_Machine learning for improved density functional theory thermodynamics.pdf
paper.research_summary: This work presents a machine learning approach to systematically correct intrinsic energy resolution errors in density functional theory (DFT) calculations of alloy formation enthalpies, improving reliability for ternary phase stability predictions. A neural network model is trained to predict the discrepancy between DFT-calculated and experimentally measured enthalpies for binary and ternary alloys and compounds, using features including elemental concentrations, atomic numbers, and interaction terms.

tasks.objective: To systematically correct intrinsic energy resolution errors in DFT-calculated formation enthalpies to improve reliability of first-principles predictions of phase stability, particularly in ternary systems.

evidence.text: In this work, we present a machine learning (ML) approach to systematically correct these errors, improving the reliability of first-principles predictions.
A neural network model has been trained to predict the discrepancy between DFT-calculated and experimentally measured enthalpies for binary and ternary alloys and compounds.
It is the purpose of this work to outline a way to reduce this error.

stages.stage_goal: Construct physically motivated input features including elemental concentrations, weighted atomic numbers, and interaction terms.

evidence.text: Each material is characterized using a structured set of input features, including elemental concentrations, atomic numbers, and interaction terms.

The final feature set consists of the original concentrations, weighted atomic numbers, and interaction terms: X = [xA, xB, xC, . . . , xAZA, xBZB, xCZC, . . . , xAB, xAC, xBC, . . . , xABC, xABD, . . .]

stages.stage_name_raw: training neural network to predict Hcorr
stages.stage_goal: Train a multi-layer perceptron regressor to map input features X to enthalpy correction Hcorr.

evidence.text: A neural network model has been implemented as a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) regressor with three hidden layers containing up to 250, 150, and 100 neurons, respectively. The predicted enthalpy correction, Hcorr, as defined in Eq. 6, is obtained as: Hcorr = f(X, θ), where f represents the neural network function with learnable network parameters θ.

stages.stage_goal: Assess predictive accuracy using LOOCV and k-fold cross-validation, measuring RMSE.
stage_output: RMSE on training and test sets

evidence.text: The model’s predictive performance has been evaluated using the root-mean-square error (RMSE) across both LOOCV and k-fold cross-validation (in this work we used five folds).

stages.stage_name_raw: comparing linear vs. neural network correction models
stages.stage_goal: Screen and compare candidate correction models (linear vs. MLP) based on RMSE and physical interpretability.

evidence.text: While the linear model offers some level of correction, its predictive power is ultimately constrained by its functional form. Even with interaction terms such as xAxB and xAxBxC, it cannot fully account for the intricate relationships governing enthalpy corrections. The neural network, in contrast, demonstrates a much greater ability to capture these relationships, leading to a substantial improvement in predictive accuracy.

stages.stage_name_raw: applying corrected enthalpies to predict phase stability
stages.stage_goal: Validate correction efficacy by computing corrected formation enthalpies (Hpred = HDFT − Hcorr) and assessing improvement in phase stability prediction.

evidence.text: The total DFT corrected enthalpy is given by Hpred = HDFT − Hcorr, where HDFT is the enthalpy from DFT calculations.

As is demonstrated below, a neural network that is trained for certain concentrations of a ternary system where Hexpt is known, can give reliable values for Hpred even for concentrations where Hexpt is missing.
